comment: Release conditions for every exact-pinned version in package.json (dependencies, devDependencies and overrides),
plus any override added to clear an npm audit advisory. An exact pin is invisible to update-npm-deps.ps1 - that
script upgrades caret ranges and skips exact versions - so nothing would ever remind you a pin is stale. This file
is what makes that check happen: on every run the script executes each `check` and compares its trimmed stdout to
`expect`. Equal means the pin is still required; different means the condition that justified the pin has changed
and the pin should be re-examined. `check: null` means no mechanical test exists - it is reported for manual review
on every run instead of going quiet. Every exact pin must have an entry here, and every entry must name a package
that is actually present in the declared section; the script reports either mismatch.

@codemirror/state.why: The version this repo's own tests run against: obsidian's peerDependencies names it exactly, so a different one would not install beside the obsidian devDependency. Consumers get the package through the caret peer (^6.5.0, the pin of obsidian 1.12.3, the bottom of the obsidian peer range), which shares their one copy - an exact runtime dependency here put a second CodeMirror state instance under the mocks for every consumer on a newer obsidian, so facets, StateFields and instanceof checks stopped matching.

@codemirror/view.why: Same as @codemirror/state - obsidian peer-pins it exactly, this is the version the tests run against, and consumers reach it through the caret peer so the view layer runs against their own CodeMirror instance.

moment.why: Must match the copy Obsidian bundles and re-exports as `moment`: obsidian's own dependencies name this exact version, and a different one would type against an API the runtime does not have. Consumers reach it through the caret peer (^2.29.4), which obsidian's own moment dependency satisfies - an exact runtime dependency here nested a second, advisory-affected moment 2.29.4 under the mocks for every consumer on obsidian 1.14.

js-yaml.why: Astro and Starlight `import yaml from 'js-yaml'`, and js-yaml 5 is ESM-only with NO default export - hoisting 5.x into their subtree makes `astro build` die on 'The requested module js-yaml does not provide an export named default' before it reads a single page. The override exists to keep the whole tree off the vulnerable 3.x line and off 4.3.1 and below, which sit inside GHSA-2883-xcg3-v3hh (maxTotalMergeKeys does not limit CPU use for empty merge sources); 4.3.2 is the patched release on the v4-legacy dist-tag, so it clears the advisory while staying loadable. It also holds markdownlint-cli2 a MAJOR below the js-yaml it exact-pins for itself - 0.23.2 declares "js-yaml": "5.2.2", and npm has no per-parent override exclusion - which is accepted rather than worked around: markdownlint-cli2 reaches js-yaml in exactly one place, `parsers/yaml-parse.mjs`, as a named `import { load } from "js-yaml"`, and js-yaml 4 exports `load` as an ESM named export, so the forced 4.3.2 loads there and `npm run lint:md` is green (verified 2026-09-15). The check tracks the v4-legacy dist-tag rather than astro's declared range because of how GHSA-2883-xcg3-v3hh surfaced in a sibling repo: on 2026-09-09 the sweep failed on it there, since 4.3.2 had shipped while this exact pin - invisible to the caret sweep by construction - sat on 4.3.1, and the astro-range check this entry used to carry stayed green the whole time. A check that cannot see the condition it guards is the silent pin that machine-re-checking every pin exists to stop.
js-yaml.manualCheck: The check is a re-examination trigger, not proof: a newer v4-legacy publish means read its changelog and move this pin onto it, because while astro is on 4.x a backport is the only way an advisory leaves this tree. The override's DELETION condition is separate and has no mechanical test here - it can go once nothing needs js-yaml 4, i.e. when `node -e "process.stdout.write(require('astro/package.json').dependencies['js-yaml'])"` stops reporting ^4.3.0. Verify either change with `npm run docs:build`, the only gate that exercises Astro's default import.

smol-toml.why: markdownlint-cli2 pins smol-toml at exactly 1.8.0 and astro / @astrojs/internal-helpers ask for ^1.6.0, so the whole tree dedupes onto 1.8.0 - which is inside GHSA-r4xh-jqrq-34v2 (<=1.8.0: quadratic-time parse() from parseKey rescanning to the end of the document on each key line). Until 2026-10-18 the override was 1.8.0, clearing GHSA-7w5x-hrqm-74c2 (<=1.7.0) while markdownlint-cli2 still pinned 1.7.0; it has since caught up to 1.8.0, but not past the second advisory. Both dependents are already on their newest release and npm audit only offers --force down to markdownlint-cli2@0.21.0, i.e. a downgrade. 1.9.1 is the newest release on the same major, so the override clears both advisories without moving anything onto an API its dependents do not use. Exact rather than caret so the sweep cannot float it onto a future 2.x that markdownlint-cli2 exact pin would reject. The check records the version markdownlint-cli2 itself asks for: when it moves onto a patched smol-toml, this override can be dropped.

katex.why: markdownlint (through markdownlint-cli2) depends on micromark-extension-math, which asks for katex ^0.16.0 and so resolves 0.16.x - inside GHSA-238p-pmpm-9mq7 (>=0.11.0 <0.18.2: existing prototype pollution can bypass trust restrictions). Every dependent is on its newest release and npm audit offers only a downgrade of markdownlint to 0.36.1, so the override forces the patched line. markdownlint uses the extension to parse math syntax only; nothing in a lint run renders math through katex, so a minor jump on a 0.x package moves no code path the lint exercises - verify with `npm run lint:md`. Exact rather than caret, like the other advisory overrides here. The check records the range micromark-extension-math asks for: when it admits a patched katex, this override can be dropped.

postcss-selector-parser.why: @astrojs/starlight reaches postcss-nested 6.2.0 through expressive-code (@expressive-code/core asks for ^6.0.1), and postcss-nested 6 asks for postcss-selector-parser ^6.1.1, which sits inside GHSA-rj75-hqrm-r3gf (<7.1.6: quadratic complexity in flat selector parsing). Starlight is on its newest release and npm audit offers only a downgrade to 0.41.11. postcss-nested 7 and later ask for ^7 with no change to how they call the parser, so the override forces the patched 7.1.6 that eslint-plugin-astro already resolves in this same tree. `npm run docs:build` is the gate that exercises it. The check records the postcss-nested range @expressive-code/core asks for: when it moves past 6.x, this override can be dropped.

fflate.why: satori pins fflate at exactly 0.7.3, which sits inside GHSA-px8p-9vwx-vf98 (0.7.0 - 0.7.4: unzipSync can enter an infinite loop on a malformed ZIP64 archive). npm audit's only offer is `--force` down to satori@0.32.0, i.e. a downgrade. 0.7.5 is the patched release on the same minor - and is already what @shuding/opentype.js resolves to in this same tree - so the override clears the advisory without moving satori off the fflate API it pins itself to. The check records the version satori itself asks for: when satori moves onto a patched fflate, this override can be dropped.

eslint-plugin-unicorn.why: `scripts/eslint-config.ts` is a hand copy of @mnaoumov/typescript-dev-toolkit's shared ESLint config, compared against it on every sweep (eslint-config-divergences.json), and the toolkit builds that config on eslint-plugin-unicorn ^76. Floating this copy to 78 (on 2026-10-18) added rules the shared config has never seen - `unicorn/no-asterisk-prefix-in-documentation-comments` alone reported 2,456 findings, against the `/** ... */` continuation style every TSDoc block here and in the toolkit uses - plus about 25 findings from other new or tightened rules. Those are decisions for the shared config to make first and this copy to follow, not ones a hand copy should make ahead of it. The check records the toolkit's unicorn range: when it moves past ^76, move this pin with it and take the new rules the way the shared config takes them.

satori.why: @mnaoumov/typescript-dev-toolkit declares satori as a peer at ^0.33.5, which for a 0.x version admits 0.33.x only, while the caret sweep floats this repo's own range to the newest satori (0.62.0 on 2026-10-18). npm refuses to resolve an optional peer present at a version its range excludes, so a floated satori makes the whole sweep UNRESOLVABLE. The toolkit's docs-site export renders the OG images with it, so it has to be a version that peer range admits. The check records the toolkit's peer range: when it moves, move this pin with it.

obsidian.why: These mocks reproduce one specific Obsidian API surface, so the type definitions they are written against are pinned rather than floated. The check records the newest published obsidian release: when it moves, the mocks should be re-examined against the new API rather than silently drifting.

typescript.why: TypeScript 7 (tsgo) breaks this toolchain: @typescript-eslint's parser crashes on the native API, so type-aware ESLint cannot run on 7. @typescript-eslint peer-requires the range below, so 6.x is the last usable major. Hold until @mnaoumov/typescript-dev-toolkit migrates.
